MoreSpace/Industries/Logistics/Shipment journey

Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the shipment journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it. Each dot is one automation.

  1. 1Enquiry & quote1 automation
  2. 2Booking & pickup request1 automation
  3. 3Vehicle & driver assignment2 automations
  4. 4Pickup, receipt & origin handling1 automation
  5. 5In transit, at hubs & at customs4 automations
  6. 6Delivery, NDR & proof of delivery2 automations
  7. 7Billing, settlement & review3 automations
1

Enquiry & quote

A shipper, importer or e-commerce brand asks for rates for a lane, a container, a monthly parcel volume or warehouse space. The same request often goes to several providers, so a complete quote on current rates, sent quickly, decides who gets the booking.

Touchpoints

  • Spot and contract rate requests by email
  • WhatsApp and website enquiries
  • Customer tender portals
  • Rate card and contract negotiations
  • New account onboarding and KYC

Accountable owner

Pricing lead or sales manager

Automations on this stage

  • Enquiry & quoteFreight RFQ-to-quote with rate cards and margin approvalRead spot and contract rate requests from email, WhatsApp and tender portals, structure them, price each lane from your own buy rates, surcharges and validity dates, and give the pricing lead a draft quote to approve before it reaches the shipper.5–8 weeks
2

Booking & pickup request

The shipper books a pickup, a container or a truck. Details captured here decide what follows: address, ready time, weight and dimensions, declared value, payment mode and whether an e-way bill or special handling is needed.

Touchpoints

  • WhatsApp and portal bookings
  • Orders pushed from seller platforms and APIs
  • Carrier booking confirmations
  • Pickup slot confirmation and labels

Accountable owner

Booking desk or customer service lead

Automations on this stage

  • Booking & pickup requestBooking and pickup scheduling on WhatsApp and the portalLet merchants book pickups through a WhatsApp Flow, the portal or an API, check serviceability, restricted items and weight before accepting, assign a pickup slot by branch cut-off, and confirm with the AWB, labels and a reminder.4–6 weeks
3

Vehicle & driver assignment

Before a vehicle is placed or a rider is sent out, operations match the load to a vehicle, confirm the driver and check licenses, permits, fitness, insurance, PUC and maintenance. A lapse found here means rescheduling; found at a checkpoint or after an accident, it means a detained vehicle or a disputed claim.

Touchpoints

  • Vehicle placement and load planning
  • Driver and rider allocation
  • Document validity checks
  • Rider and driver onboarding
  • Workshop and service scheduling

Accountable owner

Fleet or dispatch manager

Automations on this stage

  • Vehicle & driver assignmentDriver and rider onboarding with document expiry alertsCollect and verify driver and rider documents at onboarding, track every expiry date for licenses, registration, insurance, PUC, fitness and permits, and stop a vehicle or driver with a lapsed document from being assigned.4–6 weeks
  • Vehicle & driver assignmentPreventive maintenance and tire reminders from odometer dataUse GPS odometer readings and service history to schedule preventive maintenance, tire rotation and inspections for each vehicle, warn dispatch before a due vehicle is assigned, and track work orders to closure.3–5 weeks
4

Pickup, receipt & origin handling

Goods are picked up from the shipper or arrive at the hub or warehouse. They are scanned, weighed and received against the booking or ASN, and the LR, invoice and e-way bill travel with them. Discrepancies recorded here protect everyone later.

Touchpoints

  • First-mile pickup scan and weight capture
  • Dock appointment and gate entry
  • Receiving against ASN and GRN
  • LR or goods receipt and e-way bill
  • Damage and shortage photos

Accountable owner

Hub or warehouse operations manager

Automations on this stage

  • Pickup, receipt & origin handlingInbound ASN-to-GRN tracking with discrepancy alertsMatch each client's advance shipping notice with the vehicle at the dock and the goods received, flag short, excess and damaged lines with photos, and send the client a GRN summary as soon as receiving closes.4–6 weeks
5

In transit, at hubs & at customs

Line haul, hub transfers, ocean and air legs and customs clearance. Most delays happen here, documents and e-way bills must stay valid, and customers ask where their shipment is.

Touchpoints

  • GPS, hub scans and carrier milestones
  • E-way bill validity and Part B updates
  • Customs filing, queries and out of charge
  • Warehouse order cut-offs
  • Where-is-my-shipment queries

Accountable owner

Control tower or operations lead

Automations on this stage

  • In transit, at hubs & at customsE-way bill validity watch with extension and Part B alertsCompare each active e-way bill's validity with the vehicle's GPS position and ETA, warn the trip owner before expiry, prompt Part B updates when goods change vehicles, and prepare extension details for an authorized user to submit.3–5 weeks
  • In transit, at hubs & at customsCustoms document checklist and clearance status updatesBuild a document checklist for each shipment from commodity, HS code, Incoterm and destination, chase missing documents from the shipper, and keep importers and exporters updated as filing, assessment, duty payment and out of charge progress.5–8 weeks
  • In transit, at hubs & at customsProactive delay and SLA breach alerts with customer updatesWatch every shipment and warehouse order against its promised date or SLA, flag delays, stuck consignments, missed cut-offs and free-time risks early, give each exception an owner, and tell the customer before they have to ask.6–8 weeks
  • In transit, at hubs & at customsTracking-grounded support assistant on WhatsApp and webAnswer where-is-my-shipment, delivery slot, document and stock questions on WhatsApp and web chat from live tracking and WMS data, and hand over to an agent with full context whenever a person is needed.5–7 weeks
6

Delivery, NDR & proof of delivery

Out for delivery, delivered or failed. Failed attempts need a quick, honest reason and a consignee choice, and every delivery needs proof that billing and claims can rely on.

Touchpoints

  • Out-for-delivery updates
  • Delivery OTP, signature or stamp
  • Failed attempt and NDR choices
  • POD photos and unloading times
  • Shortage and damage remarks

Accountable owner

Delivery or last-mile operations manager

Automations on this stage

  • Delivery, NDR & proof of deliveryNDR resolution with consignee re-attempt choicesWhen a delivery fails, confirm the reason with the consignee, offer a re-attempt date, landmark, alternate contact or self-pickup, write the choice back to the courier platform before the next dispatch plan, and flag questionable attempts for review.4–6 weeks
  • Delivery, NDR & proof of deliveryDigital POD capture and freight invoice draftingCapture proof of delivery with photos, stamp or OTP, unloading times and remarks in the driver app or on WhatsApp, match it to the LR, and turn complete PODs into draft freight invoices with detention and other charges for finance to approve.4–6 weeks
7

Billing, settlement & review

Freight and warehouse invoices go out, COD is remitted to merchants, drivers' trip expenses are settled and clients review stock, SLAs and charges. Accuracy here decides cash flow and whether the client renews.

Touchpoints

  • Freight and storage invoices
  • COD remittances and statements
  • Driver trip settlements
  • Client stock statements and SLA reviews
  • Billing disputes and claims

Accountable owner

Finance controller with the key account manager

Automations on this stage

  • Billing, settlement & reviewCOD cash and remittance reconciliationReconcile cash-on-delivery collections from rider cash, UPI and card payments at the doorstep against delivered AWBs, flag short deposits and mismatches daily, and prepare merchant remittance files and statements for finance to release.4–6 weeks
  • Billing, settlement & reviewTrip expense and fuel claims with GPS and fuel card checksLet drivers submit fuel, toll, loading and repair expenses with receipt photos on WhatsApp, check them against fuel card, FASTag and GPS data, and give the fleet manager a short list of exceptions to approve before the trip is settled.4–6 weeks
  • Billing, settlement & reviewClient stock statements and activity-based 3PL billingSend each 3PL client scheduled stock, ageing and near-expiry statements from the WMS, and build monthly invoices from storage, handling and value-added activity under each contract, with exceptions reviewed before finance approves.4–6 weeks

Where people stay in control

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Freight RFQ-to-quote with rate cards and margin approvalEnquiry & quoteThe pricing lead approves every buy rate, margin and routing before a quote is sent, and the commercial head approves anything below the margin floor or with non-standard credit terms. The automation never commits space, rates or sailings on its own.
Booking and pickup scheduling on WhatsApp and the portalBooking & pickup requestBranch supervisors approve exceptions such as pickups after cut-off, restricted items and high-value or bulk pickups. Weight disputes are decided by the billing team using the photos and dimension records, never by the automation.
Driver and rider onboarding with document expiry alertsVehicle & driver assignmentThe fleet or HR manager approves every onboarding after reviewing flagged mismatches, and decides any exception to the assignment hold. Background verification results are reviewed by a person; the AI model only reads and compares documents.
Preventive maintenance and tire reminders from odometer dataVehicle & driver assignmentThe maintenance supervisor decides whether a defect makes a vehicle unfit to run, approves any deferral of a due service and signs off completed work orders. Brake, steering, tire and other safety-related defects reported by drivers always go to a person.
Inbound ASN-to-GRN tracking with discrepancy alertsPickup, receipt & origin handlingThe receiving supervisor confirms every discrepancy before the GRN summary is released, and the client's nominated contact decides whether to accept, return or claim against short or damaged goods. Quarantine and release of damaged or expired stock stay with the warehouse manager.
E-way bill validity watch with extension and Part B alertsIn transit, at hubs & at customsAn authorized user at the transporter reviews and submits every extension and Part B update. The automation never generates, extends or cancels an e-way bill on its own, and any interception or detention by officers is handled by the branch manager.
Customs document checklist and clearance status updatesIn transit, at hubs & at customsThe licensed customs broker reviews every document set, decides classification, valuation and exemption claims, and files and signs declarations on ICEGATE. AI flags mismatches but never changes a declaration, and the importer approves every duty payment.
Proactive delay and SLA breach alerts with customer updatesIn transit, at hubs & at customsControl-tower executives own every exception, confirm the reason before messages go to key accounts, and decide rerouting, upgrades and any cost or claim commitment. Customers are never promised compensation by an automated message.
Tracking-grounded support assistant on WhatsApp and webIn transit, at hubs & at customsSupport agents handle claims, damage reports, refunds, complaints and any change to delivery terms. The assistant states only what the data shows, says so when it does not know, and sends low-confidence answers to an agent.
NDR resolution with consignee re-attempt choicesDelivery, NDR & proof of deliveryNDR agents handle unclear replies and disputes, hub supervisors review flagged attempts and rider conduct, and the merchant decides returns for COD and high-value shipments. Address changes to another city or pin code need the merchant's approval.
Digital POD capture and freight invoice draftingDelivery, NDR & proof of deliveryThe billing executive reviews every draft invoice, and the finance controller approves detention or other charges outside the contract and any credit note. PODs with shortage or damage remarks go to the claims owner before billing.
COD cash and remittance reconciliationBilling, settlement & reviewThe finance controller approves every remittance batch before payment. Short deposits and suspected cash misuse are investigated by the branch manager and HR, never acted on by the automation, and disputed merchant deductions are held until a person decides.
Trip expense and fuel claims with GPS and fuel card checksBilling, settlement & reviewThe fleet manager approves every settlement and decides on exceptions after hearing the driver. Flags are prompts for a conversation, not findings of misconduct, and any deduction or disciplinary step is decided by the manager and HR.
Client stock statements and activity-based 3PL billingBilling, settlement & reviewThe account manager reviews exceptions and rate questions, and the finance controller approves every invoice and credit note. Decisions on near-expiry and quarantined stock, such as liquidation, return or destruction, belong to the client and are recorded against their nominated contact.
